findings.title: Ceiling-sized serialization runs on the event loop
findings.description: The async handlers put only the DB reads in `run_in_executor`; `src/manta_trading/api_server/routes/kalshi_timeseries.py:125-126` and `src/manta_trading/api_server/routes/kalshi_timeseries.py:168-174` then synchronously build the Pydantic response and call `timeseries_response` on the event-loop thread. `src/manta_trading/api_server/serialization.py:28` performs `model_dump(mode="json")` plus `orjson.dumps`/`msgpack.packb`, which is CPU-bound and far above the required <1 ms bound for synchronous work inside an `async def`; `src/manta_trading/constants.py:1285-1310` records a 75,000-row candle response at 34.80 MB. Move model construction and serialization into an executor/thread (or otherwise return the bytes without blocking the loop), and add a concurrency assertion that another request is not starved during a ceiling-sized response.

findings.title: Load tier prod-URL guard is skipped and not multiline-aware
findings.description: The new load-test docstring at `test/load/test_188_kalshi_api_nfr.py:45-50` claims the production-URL guard enforces safety mechanically, but the guard at `test/load/test_167_data_status_nfr.py:214-241` scans `splitlines()` and only flags a line containing both the variable name and an env-read marker; that misses the exact multiline `os.environ.get(\n "MT_TIMESCALE_DB_URL")` shape the project rules call out. `test/_prod_url_guard.py:32-36` has the required multiline-aware regex and `test/_prod_url_guard.py:39-55` exposes the shrink-only ratchet, but the load tier does not call it; integration and unit tiers do at `test/integration/test_integration_prod_url_guard.py:60` and `test/unit/test_unit_prod_url_guard.py:34`. The old guard is also hidden behind the module-level `MT_RUN_LOAD_TESTS` skip at `test/load/test_167_data_status_nfr.py:55-56`, so normal test runs do not execute the safety check at all. Wire the load tier to `assert_ratchet` in an unskipped guard test.

findings.title: Load tests for network/concurrency paths are not gated by CI
findings.description: `test/load/test_188_kalshi_api_nfr.py:37-47` explicitly documents that the load tier is manual-only and “Nothing here is enforced by CI today,” and `test/load/test_188_kalshi_api_nfr.py:80-86` skips the module unless `MT_RUN_LOAD_TESTS=1`. The inspected `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1-20` is publish-on-tag only and has no test job. This slice adds API/network/concurrency paths with large-response and pool-contention risks, and the Additional Review Rules require CI to gate load tests for those paths; a manual-only suite does not satisfy that requirement. Add a CI job that runs the gated load tier for affected slices.

findings.title: Time-series documentation contradicts stored schema and watermark semantics
findings.description: `src/manta_trading/api_server/models/kalshi_timeseries.py:5-10` and `src/manta_trading/data/kalshi/serve_timeseries.py:72` describe “fourteen” candle value columns, but the repository mapping and migration at `src/manta_trading/market/schema/migrations/kalshi.py:308-329` store sixteen values: fourteen nested OHLC/price fields plus `volume_fp` and `open_interest_fp`. Separately, `src/manta_trading/api_server/models/kalshi_timeseries.py:188-192` describes `tape_complete_through` as “Created time of the newest stored trade,” while the schema comment at `src/manta_trading/market/schema/migrations/kalshi.py:444-446` defines `sync_state['trades'].watermark_ts` as “the tape is complete through this instant … NOT the newest stored trade.” These are public response-model descriptions and should match the persisted semantics consumers rely on.

findings.title: Shared ceiling admission logic is duplicated between route modules
findings.description: `src/manta_trading/api_server/routes/kalshi_timeseries.py:66-78` reimplements `_admit_rows` from `src/manta_trading/api_server/routes/kalshi_catalog.py:81-94`; both enforce the same configured row ceiling, status code, error prefix, and number formatting, differing only in the advice string (“narrow start/end” vs “narrow the filter”). This violates the project’s DRY/single-source rule: a policy or error-shape change now has two edit points. Extract a shared helper that accepts the remediation text or a small enum/constant for the advice.

findings.title: Trade-row boundary is untyped and positionally restated
findings.description: `src/manta_trading/data/kalshi/serve_timeseries.py:80-82` declares `TradeRow.values` as `tuple[Any, ...]`, and `src/manta_trading/api_server/models/kalshi_timeseries.py:163-176` hard-codes `values[0]` through `values[7]` into Pydantic fields with specific `datetime`, `str`, `Decimal`, and `bool` types. The candle path deliberately follows `CANDLE_COLUMNS` at `src/manta_trading/api_server/models/kalshi_timeseries.py:76-99`, but the trade path restates column order as magic indexes, so a new or reordered `TRADE_COLUMNS` entry is not caught by the type checker and may only fail late during response validation. Use a typed DTO or build `TradeRecord` from the same column mapping used by the reader, with a parity test on field-to-column mapping rather than only row length.

structured_findings.summary: Ceiling-sized serialization runs on the event loop
Load tier prod-URL guard is skipped and not multiline-aware
Load tests for network/concurrency paths are not gated by CI
Time-series documentation contradicts stored schema and watermark semantics
Shared ceiling admission logic is duplicated between route modules
Trade-row boundary is untyped and positionally restated
